title: Why ReLU? A Bit-Model Dichotomy for Deep Network Training

claims.text: Theorem 1.1 proves that deciding ERM_bit for deep networks with any non-linear polynomial activation of degree at least 2 is #P-hard (Section 1.1, Theorem 1.1).

Corollary 1.2 shows that if ERM_bit for polynomial-activation networks were in NP, the polynomial hierarchy would collapse to its second level, evidencing intractability beyond NP (Section 1.1, Corollary 1.2).

Theorem 1.3 establishes that for polynomial activations, deciding a specific bit of the gradient is #P-hard and determining its sign is not in BPP under standard complexity assumptions (Section 1.1, Theorem 1.3).

Theorem 1.4 shows that for ReLU (piecewise-linear) activations, ERM_bit is NP-complete, while verifying a witness and computing the exact gradient via standard backpropagation both run in polynomial time (Section 1.1, Theorem 1.4).
The polynomial-activation hardness results are proved via reductions from straight-line program (SLP) problems (Section 3).
